selection: Same operator and same session-derived cases as mi355x_vllm_hip_paged_attention_decode, but the target language is FlyDSL: the AITER HIP implementation is the correctness oracle and the speedup baseline, and the agent must produce an equivalent FlyDSL kernel. Keeping the case list identical makes the two tasks directly comparable (same-language optimization vs rewrite).

provenance.shared_workload: All four sessions ran the same harness: TP=1, EP=1, concurrency=64, ISL=1024, OSL=1024, max_model_len=6144, NUM_PROMPTS=776. Decode batch is therefore 64 sequences and per-sequence KV context grows across 1024..2048 tokens. num_seqs and ctx_len are reconstructed from that regime: the graph-captured decode launches carry no recorded tensor shapes in the trace.
provenance.shared_dtypes: Every session reported kv_cache_dtype=auto, i.e. BF16 Q / KV cache / output, cross-checked against the kernels' own (vllm::Fp8KVCacheDataType)0 = kAuto template argument. Qwen3-14B-FP8 quantizes weights, not the KV cache.
provenance.head_geometry_source: Head counts read from each model's config.json under /shared_nfs/hyperloom/models and cross-checked against the GQA_RATIO template argument recorded in each trace.

models.geometry: 32 q heads / 8 kv heads / head_dim 128, 32 layers -> gqa_ratio 4
32 q heads / 8 kv heads / head_dim 128, 36 layers -> gqa_ratio 4
models.no_dedicated_cases: Geometry, dtypes and workload are identical to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (32/8/128, block_size 16, BF16, concurrency 64, ISL/OSL 1024), so the llama3_1-8b-* cases cover this model exactly. Adding duplicate case ids would only double suite runtime.

models.geometry: 16 q heads / 8 kv heads / head_dim 128, 28 layers -> gqa_ratio 2
40 q heads / 8 kv heads / head_dim 128, 40 layers -> gqa_ratio 5
models.note: The only one of the four whose session already ran the MFMA16 variant (gqa_ratio 5 > 4), so it is the closest match to what this task actually measures.

provenance.mfma_variant_caveat: Three of the four sessions (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-0.6B) ran vLLM's MFMA4 variant, selected because gqa_ratio <= 4 (see the 'mfma4 kernel is faster than mfma16 for gqa_ratio <= 4' switch in csrc/rocm/attention.cu). vLLM ships no csrc in the runtime image (wheel-only install; /app/vllm holds only benchmarks/docker/examples), so there is no in-image vLLM source to seed and edit. AITER ships the same paged_attention_ll4mi family with full source, but dispatches MFMA16 for every gqa_ratio - the MFMA4 launches are commented out in both csrc/kernels/attention.cu and csrc/cpp_itfs/pa/pa.cpp.jinja. This task therefore measures AITER's MFMA16 implementation of the same logical operator at each session's exact shapes and dtypes. Only the Qwen3-14B-FP8 cases match the session's MFMA variant as well. Verified: mfma4 symbols exist only in vllm/_rocm_C.abi3.so; aiter/jit/module_pa*.so carry mfma16 only.
provenance.specializations: compile_template_op keys on (gqa_ratio, head_size, npar_loops, dtype, kv_dtype, out_dtype, block_size, alibi, mtp, quant_method, v_shuffle). All cases give max_num_partitions = ceil(ctx_len/256) <= 8 with warpSize 64, hence npar_loops=1 - matching the sessions' paged_attention_ll4mi_reduce_kernel<..., 128, 128, 256, 1>. The suite therefore builds exactly three specializations, one per gqa_ratio (2, 4, 5).
provenance.case_density: The primary model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the largest single hot kernel across these sessions) is sampled at three context lengths to expose the memory-bound scaling; the coverage models are sampled at the two endpoints of their decode regime.

rewrite_contract.launch_signature: launch_fn(out, query, key_cache, value_cache, block_tables, seq_lens, scale) -> None (writes out in place)

tensor_layouts.key_cache: (num_blocks, num_kv_heads, head_size//x, block_size, x) bf16 with x = 16 // itemsize = 8
tensor_layouts.out: (num_seqs, num_q_heads, head_size) bf16, written in place

rewrite_contract.semantics: Decode paged attention with one query token per sequence: for each sequence s and query head h, attend over the first seq_lens[s] KV positions gathered through block_tables[s], with softmax scale `scale` and GQA sharing num_q_heads/num_kv_heads query heads per KV head. No ALiBi, no sliding window, no FP8 KV cache.
rewrite_contract.free_choices: The FlyDSL port owns its own partitioning strategy. Unlike the AITER source it is NOT handed exp_sums / max_logits / tmp_out scratch buffers, so whether to split the KV dimension and how to reduce is entirely up to the implementation.
rewrite_contract.source_reference: aiter_meta/csrc/cpp_itfs/pa/pa.cpp.jinja (launch contract and template parameters); the device code is in the sibling pa.cuh / pa_kernels.cuh / pa_common.cuh
